name: RN4871-I_RM130
title: Bluetooth Low Energy modules RN4870, RN4870U, RN4871, RN4871U
summary: A family of Bluetooth 5.0 Low Energy modules with the stack on board, controlled with ASCII commands over UART or run alone from scripts. The RN4871 is 9 × 11.5 mm with 16 pads, a shield and a ceramic chip antenna; the RN4870 is the 33-pad version with more I/O, and the U versions drop the antenna and shield for an external antenna on BT_RF. They run from 1.9 V to 3.6 V and send at 0 dBm.

notes: XXX is the firmware version; RN4871-I/RM130 carries firmware 1.30.

circuits.title: Power scheme with an LDO and a host MCU
circuits.description: One 3.3 V LDO feeds both the module's VBAT and the host MCU's VDD, so the two run at the same voltage. The module's UART TXD goes to the MCU's RX and its RXD comes from the MCU's TX. A reset IC sits across the LDO input. An LED from the 3.3 V rail is sunk by P0_2/LED, and P2_0 is the system-configuration input. Control and indication lines between module and MCU are configurable.

parts.note: drawn for RN4870, RN4871 and RN4870U

notes: VDD_IO and the MCU's VDD must be compatible.
Low-power use needs the UART_RX_IND function switched on, with that pin grounded.

circuits.title: RN4871U power scheme with an LDO and a host MCU
circuits.description: The RN4871U version of the LDO scheme. The 3.3 V rail feeds VBAT, BK_IN and the MCU's VDD, with 10 µF X5R on VBAT. The reset IC's output drives the module's reset. The LED runs from the rail through 330 Ω and is sunk by P0_2/LED. UART crosses to the MCU as before.
notes: The 10 µF X5R capacitor and the 330 Ω resistor are required.
BK_IN is tied to VBAT on the RN4871U.
Low-power use needs the UART_RX_IND function switched on, with that pin grounded.

circuits.title: Coin-cell power scheme
circuits.description: The module runs straight from a button cell: the cell's positive terminal feeds VBAT (and BK_IN on the RN4871U) with 10 µF to ground. A reset IC powered from the cell drives the module's reset. P2_0 is the system-configuration input; the multi-function I/Os (ADC, PWM on the RN4870, I2C) serve peripheral devices.
notes: Only the RN4871U needs the BK_IN connection.
Low-power use needs the UART_RX_IND function switched on, with that pin grounded.

circuits.title: External programming header
circuits.description: The five connections an external configuration and programming tool needs: P2_0, VBAT, the UART receive and transmit lines, and ground. Bringing these out on the host board is advised for development.

parts.note: same connections on every family member

circuits.title: RN4870 reference circuit
circuits.description: The RN4870 wired as a stand-alone node. Power enters at J1 and passes the STS2301 P-channel MOSFET, which blocks a reversed supply, onto VCC, held up by 10 µF. The output of an MCP111-195 reset IC, pulled up to VCC by 4.7 kΩ, drives RST. J2 brings out P2_0 (low: test mode, high: application mode), VCC, the two UART lines and ground for configuration and firmware loading. An optional LED with 330 Ω from VCC is sunk by P0_2. The remaining configurable pins are brought out as labels. VDD_IO, ULPC_O and BK_O are left open.

parts.note: P-channel MOSFET, reverse-voltage protection; drawn pin 1 drain (input), 2 gate, 3 source (VCC)

circuits.title: Power-drop protection
circuits.description: A reset IC powered from VBAT drives RST_N. The reset IC has an open-drain output, trips at 1.8 V supply and has a delay of 10 ms or less; it guards against the supply falling below the module's 1.9 V minimum.

parts.note: same connection on every family member
open drain, 1.8 V threshold, delay ≤ 10 ms

operation.text: Four modules share one Bluetooth 5.0 Low Energy design and one command set. The RN4870 (12 × 22 mm, 33 pads) and RN4871 (9 × 11.5 mm, 16 pads) are shielded and carry a ceramic chip antenna; the RN4870U (12 × 15 mm, 30 pads) and RN4871U (6 × 8 mm, 17 pads) are unshielded and bring the radio out on BT_RF for an external antenna. Suffix -V parts run from -20 °C to +70 °C, -I parts from -40 °C to +85 °C. The three digits after RM give the firmware version: RM130 is version 1.30.

An 8051 core at 16 MHz runs the Bluetooth stack from 32 KB ROM and 256 KB flash with 24 KB SRAM and 512 B of retention RAM; AES128, DMA, a watchdog and a 12-bit ADC sit beside it. Clocks are a 32 MHz crystal and a 32 kHz RC oscillator. Power is handled by a DC-DC converter, LDOs, a battery detector and a temperature sensor. Toward a host or peripherals the module offers UART, SPI, I2C, PWM, ADC inputs and an event counter.

The host drives the module with ASCII commands over UART. The commands cover connecting, scanning, bonding and the white list; reading and writing I2C, EEPROM settings, pin functions, GPIO states, analog values and PWM (RN4870 only); reboot, factory reset, command mode and low-power mode; scripts and event handlers; GATT and private services; GAP roles (central, peripheral, observer, broadcaster); advertising, scan response and beacon content; transparent UART; and configuration over the air. A script engine lets the module run without a host.

P2_0 is read at start-up. Left high (it has a pull-up) the module boots into application mode; held low it enters test mode, which is used to update flash and configure EEPROM. The RN4870's configuration pins can also be set from the BLEDK3 Windows tool.

After power is applied or an external reset pulse ends, the module samples P2_0 within the first 25 ms. Counted from the power-up or reset edge, the UART is ready for the host at 46 ms in test mode and at 68 ms in application mode; in application mode the module then signals readiness on its status pins or with a message over UART. The reset input needs a low pulse of at least 63 ns.

Low battery indication: output pulled low when VDD falls below a threshold kept in EEPROM. Status 1 and Status 2: together encode power-on, standby, connected and transparent-UART session. RSSI indication: goes low when link RSSI drops under an EEPROM threshold. Link drop: a low of 10 ms or more while connected makes the module drop the link and shut down. Pairing key: a low of 160 ms or more while connected makes the module drop the link and return to standby. RF active indication: marks when the radio is sending or receiving.

Normally the module runs from its 16 MHz clock. The command SO,1 enables low-power mode, in which it runs from the 32 kHz clock and its UART is stopped. To talk to it, the host pulls the UART RX indication pin low, which restarts the 16 MHz clock and the UART, and waits at least 5 ms before sending. For low-power designs the UART RX indication function is switched on and its pin grounded.
P2_7 falls before the module sends on UART_TX and rises when it is done, so the host can tell when data is coming.

The supply may be anything from 1.9 V to 3.6 V, and VDD_IO equals it. An LED on P0_2 needs a supply above 3.0 V. A battery-powered design should add reverse-polarity protection. The RN4870U needs an antenna matching network on BT_RF. With an LDO, one 3.3 V rail for module and host MCU keeps their logic levels equal.
Below 1.9 V the module may misbehave, so a reset IC is advised: open-drain output, delay of 10 ms or less, tripping at 1.8 V, driving RST_N.

Keep top copper away from the test-pad keep-out areas. Under the antenna no copper may lie on any layer. A low-impedance ground plane gives the best range and lowest noise; the RN4870 wants at least 4.7 mm of ground to the left and 6.4 mm to the right of the module, and the RN4871 a clear space around its antenna section; the plane may be made larger for EMC. Keep other metal at least 30 mm from the ceramic antenna. Range measured in open air to a phone: up to 50 m for the RN4870, up to 10 m for the RN4871.

BT_RF on the RN4870U and RN4871U is a 50 Ω port for a PCB trace antenna, a chip antenna or a 50 Ω microstrip on the host board. The trace may carry pads for attenuation, matching or test posts. Keep it as short as possible; a longer trace should be 50 Ω. Place the RN4871U at the board edge for the best transmit and receive performance.

The modules are built with a lead-free reflow profile to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 and accept leaded or lead-free reflow. Peak temperature must stay at or under 250 °C. Use no-clean paste and do not wash, since moisture can stay under the shield. Reflow the module once only; on a board that sees several passes, place it in the last.

Built in: the Device Information public service and the Transparent UART private service for streaming data. Users can define up to five public and four private services, each with up to eight characteristics, held in non-volatile memory so they are set up once. A private service works only with peers that implement it too.

The modules hold modular approvals for the US (FCC Part 15 Subpart C), Canada, Europe (RED), UK (UKCA), Japan, Korea, Taiwan and China, and the RN4871 also for Brazil. The approvals rely on the antennas listed for each module; another antenna is allowed only if it is the same type with equal or lower gain and comparable behaviour inside and outside the band.
